Use the actual photographed MYJG-40NW P2 second G/IN/5V group only if the fitted model and terminal view match. Prime P12 J35.6 is a sourced PWM contact, not a qualified direct 5 V PSU input. TI allows AHCT VCC 4.5–5.5 V, but Cloudray limits IN PWM peak to 5.0 V: select and measure a separately rated 4.5–5.0 V rail including tolerance, ripple and transients, or redesign the output limiting stage. Its logic 0 V, Prime J35.10 and photographed P2 second G form a proposed shared reference ONLY after cabinet common/PE/noise isolation checks. PSU P2 5V remains UNUSED; the manual's separate P3 5V row conflicts with its own 24 V description, so no PSU accessory rail is qualified. Require configured PWM frequency at least 20 kHz, measured peak at most 5.0 V at P2 IN, receiver current within the buffer's recommended output current, and no fire on power-up, reset, disconnect or process-off. The buffer is not galvanic isolation or a safety interlock. Keep the independent water/door/E-stop chain and separate K+/K- firing circuit in the next panel.

wire_panels.title: K40 MYJG-40NW photographed P2 · conditional isolated K+ fire and independent protection
wire_panels.note: CONDITIONAL MANUFACTURER REFERENCE, not verified fitted laser PSU. Slow process-fire request is distinct from ≥20 kHz intensity PWM. Prime J35.7 PWM.2 is sourced as a TTL-labelled candidate but its carrier drive, polarity and startup default are UNQUALIFIED. ULN2003AN sinks a current-limited AQY212GS LED from the same separately qualified 4.5–5.0 V external rail used by the PWM panel. AQY212GS normally open contact is proposed ONLY across photographed P2 K+ and K-; P3 L and later TH/TL are mutually exclusive alternate functions and are UNUSED here. Qualify actual K+ open voltage ≥3 V (inhibit), closed voltage ≤0.3 V (fire), K+ input current against AQY output/on-resistance/off-leakage, AQY LED current 5–10 mA over tolerance, boot/reset/disconnect states, and fitted connector orientation before installation. The AQY output is a slow command contact, never 20 kHz PWM or a safety-rated E-stop/STO. Do not add a host-GND wire to K-; both photographed P2 G and K- are enclosure-grounded per the manual, so component isolation does not establish system galvanic separation. Trace all cabinet bonds. Separate water/door/key/E-stop chain into photographed P2 P+/first G remains OPEN until every fitted contact and fail-safe behavior is traced; never bridge protection or energize the laser from this proposal. ULN2003AN unused inputs pins 2–7 are defined low at pin 8 logic GND; unused collector outputs pins 10–15 and COM pin 9 remain NC for the LED load. These are host-side component terminations, not K- field wiring.

instructions: Match the actual machine and controller revisions, trace the unpowered harness and verify all signal/reference, power and independent safety boundaries before energising. Follow the current connection IDs rather than the superseded architecture prose.

X min limit · signal and ground separately: Trace cable with power isolated; confirm dry contact and NO/NC state. Leave selector pin 1 unused for passive switches; powered sensors require a matched interface.

Y min limit · signal and ground separately: Trace cable with power isolated; confirm dry contact and NO/NC state. Leave selector pin 1 unused for passive switches; powered sensors require a matched interface.

K40 laser power supply · control and reference: G/IN/5V are source labels. Confirm the fitted PSU model, input threshold and compatible level interface; the Mini Gerbil installation is not evidence of direct Prime 3.3 V compatibility. Laser firing enable is a separate circuit, not supplied by intensity PWM.

Alternative L/LO-labelled PSU firing boundary · mutually exclusive with TL variant: Identify active level, firing terminal and water/door/key/E-stop contacts from the fitted PSU manual. Retain the independent hardware inhibition chain; do not bridge an interlock. PSU 5V is an output/reference, not a Prime PWM pin. Choose the installed PSU variant only: the L/LO and TH/TL reference labels are alternatives, not two firing connections to install together.

Prime selected · X onboard driver output: Selected replacement: integrated driver outputs directly to motor winding pairs. Verify selected Prime revision, current settings, supply rating and winding pairs.

Prime selected · Y onboard driver output: Selected replacement: integrated driver outputs directly to motor winding pairs. Verify selected Prime revision, current settings, supply rating and winding pairs.

Prime selected · separate logic and motor supplies: This is the selected Prime P12 integrated-driver architecture. Use the current P12 PCB-derived contact labels; other board revisions require their own verified pinout and driver ratings. Use one verified power-entry arrangement; J10 parallels VMOT and is left unused here. Board ground is shared internally; route motor current directly to power distribution, not through logic wiring. Determine actual allowed voltage/current before choosing a supply; no machine-source adapter automatically qualifies.

Laser protection and firing inputs · match fitted PSU variant: Cloudray MYJG-40 NW is a reference variant only, not proof of installed PSU. Its manual distinguishes TH/TL firing, WP water/fan protection, G reference and IN intensity. Follow matching manufacturer isolation and active-level requirements; do not bridge WP or remove water/door/E-stop checks. Existing L/LO labels elsewhere describe other possible PSU variants.

New conditional photographed-P2 PWM panel: identify the fitted PSU nameplate and P2 connector orientation, then qualify external 5 V rail, Prime J35.6 electrical output and J35.10/common bond. Require measured ≥20 kHz PWM, ≤5.0 V peak at P2 IN including tolerance/transients, receiver current within AHCT limit, and safe boot/reset/process-off behavior. The PSU auxiliary 5V output is unused.

New conditional photographed-P2 fire panel: use only the slow J35.7/ULN2003AN/AQY212GS contact proposal across P2 K+/K-. Verify AQY LED current 5–10 mA, K+ open ≥3 V and closed ≤0.3 V at fitted input current, and loss-of-power inactive behavior. Do not join a second P3 L or later TH/TL fire path. Component isolation does not prove whole-cabinet galvanic separation.

Keep photographed P2 P+/first G water/door/key/E-stop path OPEN until each fitted series contact, polarity and power source is traced. Neither the conditional PWM buffer nor AQY command contact is a safety interlock or permission to energize the laser.

wire_panels.note: CONDITIONAL REFERENCE ONLY, not verified CubeFactory fitted hotend sensor or cable. CubeFactory identifies a BQ Prusa i3 Hephestos printer. The bq Hephestos Marlin Configuration.h selects TEMP_SENSOR_0 99; its matching thermistortables.h table 99 is a 100 kΩ curve (historically commented as a bed thermistor), not generic Marlin table 1 and not proof of this machine's installed sensor. Connect a physically identified, measured matching two-lead NTC only: one lead to Prime P12 J21.1 temperature sensor input, the other to J21.2 GND. Lead A/B are logical names, not source-assigned harness cavities; an NTC is nonpolar. The pinned Prime P12 schematic/netlist and BOM put RN3 4.7 kΩ pull-up from J21.1 to /3V3, C49 1 µF from J21.1 to GND, RN4 4.7 kΩ series toward U12 LMV324 conditioning, and J21.2 on GND. The specified source hardware does not prove fitted component population, controller firmware sensor channel, ADC transfer, sensor curve or safe heater behavior. Do not add an external pull-up by assumption; inspect the actual board and calculate/configure the complete front-end transfer for the measured sensor. Keep J17 Hotend A heater power disabled until ambient and independently checked heated-point readings, open/short faults, firmware thermal shutdown and an independently rated thermal cutoff pass. The recycler Inkbird heater stays a separate control system.

target_options.core: V2 Core has no integrated stepper power stages; add four selected external stepper drivers and measure each motor winding/current. Core J5 A–D STEP/DIR are logical signals; slash-prefixed net names do not mean active-low.
target_options.prime: Selected main reference: Prime P12 integrated four printer motor channels and researched P12 heater/fan/temperature candidates. Retain recycler ESCON and independently controlled sleeve heater; verify fitted harness, motor/heater/sensor ratings and firmware support.

instructions: Match the actual machine and controller revisions, trace the unpowered harness and verify all signal/reference, power and independent safety boundaries before energising. Follow the current connection IDs rather than the superseded architecture prose.

Printer X stepper · integrated Prime driver channel A: Four phase conductors are shown separately. The Prime PCB exposes these phase outputs, but CubeFactory installed motor cable colours, winding pairs, and board revision are not documented. Verify current/supply limits before connecting.

Printer Y stepper · integrated Prime driver channel B: Four phase conductors are shown separately. The Prime PCB exposes these phase outputs, but CubeFactory installed motor cable colours, winding pairs, and board revision are not documented. Verify current/supply limits before connecting.

Printer Z stepper · integrated Prime driver channel C: Four phase conductors are shown separately. The Prime PCB exposes these phase outputs, but CubeFactory installed motor cable colours, winding pairs, and board revision are not documented. Verify current/supply limits before connecting.

Printer E stepper · integrated Prime driver channel D: Four phase conductors are shown separately. The Prime PCB exposes these phase outputs, but CubeFactory installed motor cable colours, winding pairs, and board revision are not documented. Verify current/supply limits before connecting.

Recycler · configured PWM setpoint and independent run input: Use the actual contact labels and per-wire qualification in the current main diagram. Any older Core/header reference in retained source context is not the selected controller endpoint.

Recycler · retain motor power stage and feedback on ESCON: Maxon J3 Hall schedule: 1 Hall1, 2 Hall2, 3 Hall3, 4 +5 V Hall supply (≤30 mA), 5 GND. J3 motor/Hall wiring is source-specific but the CubeFactory harness is unreported; OPEN breaks prevent fabricated phase/color assignments. ESCON 70/10 current rating must be reconciled with project claim of 10 A normal / 40 A maximum before use.

Recycler heater and original controller · do not splice yet: Project text says Inkbird D1S-2R-24, but the visible photograph only shows INKBIRD/ITC front branding. Identify rear label, sensor, supply, output rating and the 24 V supply branch; then add exact contacts.

Prime selected · separate logic and motor supplies: This is the selected Prime P12 integrated-driver architecture. Use the current P12 PCB-derived contact labels; other board revisions require their own verified pinout and driver ratings. Use one verified power-entry arrangement; J10 parallels VMOT and is left unused here. Board ground is shared internally; route motor current directly to power distribution, not through logic wiring. Determine actual allowed voltage/current before choosing a supply; no machine-source adapter automatically qualifies.

Printer home inputs · X, Y and Z switch pairs: Prusa/Hephestos family reference does not establish the fitted CubeFactory harness. This proposal uses newly identified passive switch leads; confirm each NO/NC state and firmware axis assignment with power isolated. Pin1 supply selectors stay unused. Powered sensors need an electrically matched interface, not this passive-contact circuit. Optional max inputs J25/J27/J29 remain unconnected unless actual additional switches are fitted and mapped.

Prime P12 · Hotend A · complete external power and load circuit: Board-side evidence: exact P12 schematic/PCB at commit7dc4f9a identifies J17 Hotend A, J18 Hotend B, J19 Fan1, J20 Fan2. J17.1 receives shared Q25 cutoff-controlled VFET; J17.2 is Q19 switched return. These are factory internal circuits, not user soldering instructions. PE0 / HOTEND_A_FET and PF14 / OUTPUTENABLE come from the exact P12 source; a general documentation PJ6 label conflicts and must not override this revision. Heater/sensor fitment and connector-safe current are unknown: measure, qualify firmware and prove thermal shutdown before connecting heat. No guaranteed 5A terminal rating is asserted.

Prime P12 · individual fan outputs and spare Hotend B: J19/J20 pin1 share the same VFET output from factory Q25; pin2 returns switch through Q21/Q22. No second power supply is connected to the fan outputs. Leave both J18 contacts unconnected in this one-hotend option. Actual hotend heatsink cooling must be maintained; do not assume an original fan is VFET-voltage rated.

Printer hotend temperature · feedback required before any heat: BQ reference names temperature sensing, but fitted sensor type/lead pairs are not identified. Prime J21.1/.2 supports the board temperature input and return; establish NTC/PT100/thermocouple identity and configure a compatible sensor circuit and firmware. Heater power must remain disabled until feedback, fault detection and independent cutoff are proved. The recycler Inkbird heater remains an independent controller system.

Conditional J21 thermistor reference: with heater power isolated, trace both hotend sensor leads, measure resistance at ambient and at an independently known safe temperature, and compare the full curve against bq table 99. Confirm fitted Prime P12 J21.1/J21.2, RN3/RN4/C49/U12 population, input voltage and firmware ADC transfer; configure the actual Smoothie sensor curve and channel rather than copying Marlin TEMP_SENSOR_0=99 as a preset.

Only after plausible ambient and two independent temperature points are established, verify disconnected/shorted sensor faults and independent thermal cutoff with heater power still isolated. Keep J17 Hotend A power disabled until the fitted heater, sensor, controller firmware and fault shutdown have been separately qualified. The recycler Inkbird loop is independent.

fields.target: Use Prime for the printer only after motor/heater/sensor ratings are confirmed; retain the ESCON 70/10 on the recycler and use Core PWM as a configured setpoint/run command. The heater controller remains unidentified.
fields.plan: The printer and recycler are separate systems. Prime provides four integrated stepper stages, so a measured printer motor winding pair can connect directly to the matching Prime phase outputs when the motor current and supply ratings fit. Core instead needs four selected external stepper drivers. The recycler BLDC phases and Hall feedback remain on the ESCON. Every dashed route is a proposed axis or software mapping, not a fitted-harness assertion.

Core P1 source nets: J5.16 STEP_A, .18 DIR_A, .22 STEP_B, .24 DIR_B, .28 STEP_C, .30 DIR_C, .34 STEP_D, .36 DIR_D, .13 shared MOT_EN; J35.6 TIM1_CH1, .7 TIM1_CH2, .10 GND. Slash is namespace syntax, not polarity proof.

ESCON J5: 1 DigIN1, 2 DigIN2, 3 configurable DigIN/DigOUT3, 4 configurable DigIN/DigOUT4, 5 signal GND, 6 +5 V ≤10 mA. J6: 1/2 differential AnIN1, 3/4 AnIN2, 5/6 analog outputs, 7 GND. J3 Hall: 1/2/3 H1/H2/H3, 4 +5 V ≤30mA, 5 GND.
CubeFactory motor lead cavities, printer thermistor/heater/switch contacts, fitted ZUM revision, heater controller rear terminal schedule and installed supply contacts remain unknown.

instructions: Photograph and transcribe fitted controller, ESCON, motor, supply, printer board and heater-controller labels.
Isolate power. Check ESCON current limit and motor rating against 10 A normal / 40 A maximum project statements; do not assume the 70/10 model can sustain 40 A.

For Prime, continuity-test each printer motor to identify A/B winding pairs and verify phase current and supply range; connect only to J5/J6/J7/J8 after rating check. For Core, select matching external drivers and preserve the separate driver power stage.
Verify ESCON DigIN1 PWM configuration, frequency, setpoint scaling, DigIN2 run function, reference and stop behavior before signal connection.
Leave heater, sensors and limit switches OPEN until exact fitted device and terminal function are identified. Prove physical E-stop and guards independently of Smoothie.

wire_panels.note: SmoothieBox exterior contact assignment is a proposed Chapter 18 harness; verify the fitted case and logic level. Specific electronic proposal: R1=10 kΩ, C1=10 µF, OPA197 U3 SOIC-8: pin6 OUT, pin7 V+, pin4 V−, pin3 +IN, pin2 −IN; pins1/5/8 NC, Rf=10 kΩ and Rg=10 kΩ yield nominal gain 2.0 (verified 0–5 V case PWM average -> 0–10 V). It is not isolated, is not installed hardware, and requires scope/ground-noise/transfer validation. No run/stop or safety function is provided. OPA197 SOIC-8 NC pins 1, 5 and 8 are not connected. Fit local 100 nF bypass between U3 pins7 and4, plus nearby bulk capacitance chosen for supply impedance. R1/C1 time constant is 0.1 s: verify ripple and speed response at chosen PWM frequency. Sequence supplies so GPIO does not drive an unpowered stage; prove zero-command/startup output and loss-of-command shutdown. The case reference proposes 5V PWM rather than direct 3V3 GPIO: this selected converter uses gain 2. Verify actual output amplitude/polarity, rail tolerance, clipping and transfer with VFD disconnected; do not use the earlier gain-3 Core circuit on a 5V case signal.

This proposal deliberately leaves the relay module model and source/sink selection conditional; no 24 V terminal is directly connected to Smoothie. Keep NOT-Aus/guards/contactor chain hardwired and independent. The 2.2 kW spindle power path uses correct nameplate mains/filter to VFD input and WJ200 U/T1, V/T2, W/T3 plus PE to spindle; no mains contacts are guessed here. See the separate fully named ULN2003AN/AQY212GS process-run proposal; no generic unspecified relay is needed.

pins: MSD556 Rev3.0 source P1 functions: 1 PUL+,2 PUL−,3 DIR+,4 DIR−,5 ENA+,6 ENA−; P2: GND,+V,A+,A−,B+,B−. 20–50VDC family range; 5.6A peak/4A RMS; input current 7–16mA; pulse ≤400kHz, pulse width >1.2µs, DIR setup ≥5µs; ENA typically unconnected/enabled.

SN74LVC07A SOIC-14 exact pins:1 1A,2 1Y,3 2A,4 2Y,5 3A,6 3Y,7 GND,8 4Y,9 4A,10 5Y,11 5A,12 6Y,13 6A,14 VCC; open-drain outputs accept up to 5.5V. Confirm input sink-current requirement against guaranteed TI VOL/current conditions.

guides.title: Genmitsu 3018-PROVer V2 retrofit
guides.target: Replace the integrated Genmitsu motion board with Prime P12 direct motor-phase outputs. Use the depicted separate Cytron spindle stage and qualified interfaces for probe, limits, optional laser, pump, emergency stop and unsupported factory UI.
guides.plan: Original motion-driver electronics are on the board being replaced. Use Prime integrated phase outputs directly to measured winding pairs; do not connect STEP/DIR signal outputs to motor windings. Confirm installed board, motor current and power rating from the cited machine source. Selected architecture: Prime P12 with integrated motor drivers. The main diagram and connection-ID schedule define the current proposed routes. Dotted function-coloured GUESS routes need the named commissioning checks; OPEN routes remain disconnected until the missing terminal, rating or interface is established. Previous Core alternatives remain only in the superseded historical architecture record.

parts: One StepperOnline DM320T per Core-controlled axis, with a TI SN74LVC07A six-channel open-drain buffer proposal (three buffers, one per axis (only two of six channels loaded per device)); manual exposes P1 PUL/DIR/OPTO/ENA and P2 +Vdc/GND/A+/A-/B+/B-.

instructions: Core power candidate: route the selected, fused and voltage-verified board supply to Core P1 J42.1 (/5VPORTIN) and supply return to J42.2 (GND). Check exact Core revision input range/current and upstream fuse before energizing; do not mistake J42.1 for a 5V output.
Record board/motor/PSU revision and use continuity to identify each 4-wire motor coil pair before connection.

For Core, use SN74LVC07A channels as 3.3V-input open-drain sinks: for each axis use one SN74LVC07A (STEP A1→Y1 pins1→2, DIR A2→Y2 pins3→4); pins5/6,9/8,11/10,13/12 remain unused. Power each pin14 from Core J5.10 3V3, pin7 to one verified J5 return, and fit 100nF directly across each device. DM320T PUL/DIR inputs draw 7–16mA each: two loaded sinks total 14–32mA/device, below TI 100mA package GND-current absolute maximum; verify actual input-current setting and scope pulse timing.
Set motor current from the motor nameplate, fuse every stage, and test one unloaded axis at conservative speed.
Map each individual MIN and MAX switch to its own Prime input only after continuity and NO/NC checks; do not infer connector assignment from socket placement.
Test PWM into MD10C with spindle disconnected first; then test secured spindle at low duty/current. Prove E-stop removes hazardous energy independent of firmware.

ClearPath command buffer #1: SmoothieBox STEP/DIR → AHCT125 → Avid J8/J9: SmoothieBox exterior contact assignment is a proposed Chapter 18 harness; verify the fitted case and logic level. wire_panels.title: X Home/Limit · proposed isolated sensor circuit with complete field and host wiring
wire_panels.note: Conditional proposed circuit: identify fitted M12 pin view and sensor NPN/PNP plus NO/NC type; match SJ2 and SJ1, verify sensor residual/leakage and board ratings, host pull-up, bank pin1 voltage/current, and test target response before installation. Field GF and host GND_H stay isolated. NO sensor cable breaks and wrong SJ2 in NO mode are not universally detected. This v01 PCB is not qualified. M12 position 2 is explicitly shown unresolved and has no conductor; no mating-face or sensor assignment is inferred. EX 24.1 sourced function: J7.3 X Home/Limit. The SmoothieBox input name is a proposed firmware allocation, not the name or direction of this machine sensor. J8.2 groups X/Y1/Z/Y+ on IN2 and J8.3 groups Y2/A on IN3; do not imply independent original Acorn inputs. Proposed firmware allocation XMIN. Controller connector MIN/MAX labels describe the case bank, not this sensor direction.

GP8101S PWM-high threshold is 2.7 V; fitted MCU supply/pad mode/load and output-stage implementation must establish compatibility. Keep the proposed adapter link dotted and fitted VFD endpoints unresolved.

pins: TI SN74AHCT125 14-pin pin schedule: 1=/OE1, 2=1A, 3=1Y, 4=/OE2, 5=2A, 6=2Y, 7=GND, 8=3Y, 9=3A, 10=/OE3, 11=4Y, 12=4A, 13=/OE4, 14=VCC. Each active-low OE must be deliberately controlled; low enables A-to-Y.

Core→Avid: J5.16 STEP_A -> buffer1 input -> J8.1 X STEP; J5.18 DIR_A -> buffer1 -> J8.2 X DIR; J5.22 STEP_B -> buffer1 -> J8.3 Y STEP; J5.24 DIR_B -> buffer1 -> J8.4 Y DIR; J5.28 STEP_C -> buffer2 -> J9.1 Z STEP; J5.30 DIR_C -> buffer2 -> J9.2 Z DIR; J5.34 STEP_D -> buffer2 -> J9.3 A STEP; J5.36 DIR_D -> buffer2 -> J9.4 A DIR. All eight routes are proposals until current input references/timing are verified.
Enable candidate: Core J5.13 /MOT_EN -> third AHCT125 channel -> Avid J12.1 ENA1; polarity/fanout/reset state unresolved. J12.2/3 are jumper-derived Y step routes, not enable.
Avid servo cable connectors J1=X,J2=Y1,J3=A,J4=Y2,J5=Z each have pins1 HLFB+,2-4 +5V,5 HLFB-,6 STEP,7 DIR,8 ENABLE per Avid 24.1 source. This is retained Avid-side wiring, not direct Core wiring.
Smoothieboard V2 Core P1 J42 candidate supply inlet: pin1=/5VPORTIN, pin2=GND (exported board contacts). Verify exact board-revision supply specifications before connection; pin1 is not a 5V output.
parts: Three TI SN74AHCT125 14-pin buffers as a test-gated level-interface proposal: two devices route eight STEP/DIR lines, one channel on the third carries an enable candidate. Select 14-pin package documented by TI; provide verified 5V, decoupling, and safe /OE control.
If Core return and Avid J7.1 COM cannot be safely joined, use a pulse interface that provides galvanic isolation and matches Avid receiver characteristics.
Retain Avid CRP5310-01E and ClearPath wiring only if installed revision/cables match the 24.1 schedule. Keep hardware E-stop independent.
instructions: Inspect CRP board silkscreen, J8/J9/J12/J13/J10 state and motor cable options; do not infer rev from machine model.

Build and bench-check each AHCT125: pin14=regulated 4.5–5.5V, pin7=GND, one 100nF directly across each IC supply pair, and all four /OE pins per chip deliberately set. Verify power-up/reset behavior with servo power disabled. Confirm Core 3.3V VIH meets TI AHCT125 VIH and output loading is within limits.
Verify Core and Avid signal references; use isolated pulse interface if a safe common is not established. Never assume J7.1 COM can be tied to Core return.
Connect and scope one STEP/DIR channel at a time to J8/J9; verify pulse width/setup, no boot glitches and axis mapping before servo enable.
Enable only under bounded safe test; validate Y2 J12 jumper path and J13 inversion, HLFB and faults, then prove hardwired E-stop. Keep VFD/plasma disabled pending exact peripherals.

instructions: Confirm actual board revision and photograph both PCB sides/cable headers before changing wiring.
Measure each motor winding pair and identify each cavity; set current and test one axis at a time.
Read E3D sensor and heater part markings; measure cold sensor resistance and heater resistance. Match firmware curve/amplifier and heater voltage/current before applying heat.

Keep hotend heater power OPEN until its board output, rail, wiring, fuse, thermal fuse and connector ratings are source-verified.

Identify every fan voltage/current and all six limit/probe contacts; test NO/NC and signal range. Verify plausible ambient temperature, then test one heater with independent cutoff/current monitoring.

MAX31865PMB1 datasheet BOM lists installed R7=400Ω ±0.1% as its PT100 reference resistor; BIAS is internal, not a separate wiring terminal. Verify module revision and resistor population before connecting an RTD.

wire_panels.note: Independent X ENABLE control, not STO/E-stop. Configure correct drive DI ServoOn and case output polarity; prove reset/loss-of-command is off. SmoothieBox exterior contact assignment is a proposed Chapter 18 harness; verify the fitted case and logic level. New engineering proposal: SmoothieBox GPIO → ULN2003AN → AQY212GS LED, isolated contact pins3/4 to configured machine run circuit. This slow process interface does not implement E-stop, STO or PWM. Verify startup inactive, receiver mode/current, isolation layout and loaded off-state leakage before use. A nominal 390 Ω resistor gives 5.51 mA at the stated 4.75 V rail, 1.5 V LED and 1.1 V sink-drop assumptions; this calculation is not a tolerance or temperature guarantee. Verify the complete rail, resistor, LED and sink voltage ranges keep LED current within the Panasonic recommended 5–10 mA operating range. Panasonic catalog printed pages81–82 lists AQY212GS output absolute maxima of 60 V peak AC/DC and 1.0 A at25°C, with power/temperature derating; these are not unconditional working ratings. Qualify receiver current, off-state leakage, isolation layout and actual fitted device. Contact is bidirectional and galvanically isolated from the LED side: no logic ground crosses that barrier.

wire_panels.note: MANUFACTURER REFERENCE ONLY; this is not verified installed MH50V wiring. Delta ASDA-B3 manual section 3.1.3, printed p.3-6, permits the 220 V-series, 1.5 kW-or-below single-phase example only when the exact fitted drive model matches. The main input uses R and T; S is UNUSED. The two control-supply terminals L1C and L2C branch from filtered input before the MC main contacts and remain supplied when those main contacts open. The manufacturer's MCCB, noise filter and two-pole MC are functional stages; their actual cabinet models, ratings, branch protection, contact numbers, wiring method, and MC coil/interlock design are unknown. Its Power 1 NO, Power 2 NC, ALRM_RY_A NO, SPD, 24 VDC and CN1 DO circuit require model-specific DO parameters and are not reproduced as fitted control wiring here. The post-filter split is a logical net; select qualified distribution hardware rather than assuming that a filter terminal accepts multiple conductors. U/V/W are example motor phases; motor identity, cable contacts, encoder, brake and STO remain unresolved. PE is protective earth, never SmoothieBox logic GND or DC return. Keep existing axis-specific OPEN inventory and every stable edge ID until the installed drive suffix, motor nameplates and cabinet schedule are traced.

instructions: Read the model suffix on all X/Y/Z/spindle Delta drives. Confirm they are B3A-L pulse-type drives; the same-family pin numbers are not portable to other variants.

With power isolated, check every DB44 conductor for continuity, shorts between differential pair members and shorts to shields; the owner reported a crossed/melted X DIR pair that damaged a Mesa output and proximity switch.

Implement AM26LV31E diff outputs with exact pin assignments shown. Verify VCC/GND, both enable polarities, idle state and pulse pair with oscilloscope before connecting drives; test one axis while mechanically uncoupled/drive disabled.
Set/read back P1.000 differential command mode and pulse format. Do not connect 24V PULL_HI pins 35/36 in line-driver mode; never apply 24V to SIGN/PULSE pair contacts.

Read back DI/DO assignments and polarity before enabling SON/alarm/reset. Confirm safe E-stop/STO, limit switches and proximity inputs independently; do not repeat unattended homing until fault cause is corrected.
Keep servo AC, U/V/W, encoder, brake, STO and protective earth in the exact Delta machine wiring domain, never on Smoothie pins.

Either verify the exact installed drives can be configured for compatible pulse-position commands, or retain a supported closed-loop motion controller/drive architecture. No SmoothieBox-to-analog position loop is proposed.

Pneumatic backgear: valve identity and stopped-spindle interlock required: SmoothieBox exterior contact assignment is a proposed Chapter 18 harness; verify the fitted case and logic level. Owner says gear changes only with spindle stopped, and no gear-position sensor is fitted/reported. Planned 7i84/brake outputs were not confirmed installed. Identify manifold station and coil; add independent spindle-stopped permissive before any actuation.

Preserve existing physical spindle/safety controls until traced and verified: SmoothieBox exterior contact assignment is a proposed Chapter 18 harness; verify the fitted case and logic level. Thread reports damaged spare Mesa 7i84 and planned quick-stop/brake at cited time; current installation unknown. Do not label planned parts as installed. Keep safety and contactor logic independent of Smoothie. The named physical controls and safety functions are retained for tracing; no controller-to-contactor or forward-to-E-stop wire is proposed.

Spindle speed and run · SmoothieBox interface proposal: Owner reports original 0–10V speed mode and VFD Pin28 enable. Identify fitted VFD model, analog range/return, enable circuit and safe stop behavior. Proposed PWM-to-0–10V conversion and isolated run contact are process control only; not a replacement for the retained spindle safety and closed-loop axis control.

Schaublin JASD conditional branch: record each installed X/Z JMC drive and motor nameplate, CN1 face/numbering, supply rating and motor/encoder harness before using the recovered v1.3 mirror. The deleted owner-linked manual was not byte-verified against this mirror. If fitted models differ, keep old panel 3 OPEN and the established LinuxCNC/Mesa analog architecture.

With motor power isolated, configure and read back fitted drive P01-01=0 position, P03-00=0 pulse command, P03-01=1 direction+pulse and P03-02=0 low-speed inputs only when supported; verify pulse polarity, electronic gearing, direction, maximum 500 kHz and all independent overtravel/stop behavior. Do not use 24 V CN1.39/.35 together with 5 V CN1.43/.36.

Bench-qualify the AM26C31 adapter: 4.5–5.5 V at pin16/pin8, 0.1 µF bypass, SmoothieBox DRVX/DRVZ VOH/VOL and reference, pull-down loading, 5 V differential opto current within TI ±20 mA recommended output range, twisted-pair cable, edge timing and boot/reset/disconnect pulses with servo inhibited.

Trace existing JASD power and motor circuits; only qualified model-specific 220 V main/control feeds may populate the R/S/T and L1/L2 reference. Preserve U/V/W phase identity, motor PE and matched CN2 encoder cable. Do not bridge B1/B2 or attach an external resistor until exact regenerative model and rating are established.

For each axis, read back installed P06-00/P06-01 before Servo ON. Qualify DRVX/DRVZ ENABLE VOH/VOL/current, ULN threshold/saturation, proposed 10 kΩ boot-low bias, 390 Ω LED current at 5–10 mA, AQY contact off leakage/on resistance and default-open behavior against actual DI1 current and 24 V polarity. Keep the 24 V DI return separated from controller/ULN 0 V and PE in the proposal; trace actual cabinet bonds. Keep independent safety/contactors/E-stop. No analog DAC position-loop or synchronized lathe threading claim.

Conditional Lenze digital RUN/DIR: identify fitted Lenze8214 nameplate and terminal schedule; qualify manufacturer SHB0199 8200-family text and owner post338649. Configure/test SSR1.1 RUN and PWM.2 TTL direction with measured output levels/current and inactive boot/reset/disconnect behavior. Qualify ULN sink and Phoenix coil24V A1/A2 polarity/current, field contact intact-gold 1mA-at24V to50mA/36VDC limits, Lenze28/E4 HIGH12–30V LOW0–3V with proposed10kΩ pull-downs, GND2 terminal39 return and actual rotation/configuration. Preserve analog terminal7/GND1 isolation, unused terminal20 and independent safety/contactors. Do not infer K11/K12 alarm feedback from conflicting source labels.

wire_panels.title: CONDITIONAL JASD v1.3 X/Z position command · SmoothieBox → AM26C31 → 5 V CN1 differential inputs
wire_panels.note: MANUFACTURER CONDITIONAL REFERENCE; not a verified fitted Schaublin drive, motor, cabinet or harness. Owner post #259199 says the JMC drives run in analog mode and considers temporary STEP/DIR position-mode tuning. Match both physical drive nameplates, revision and CN1 schedule to this recovered JASD v1.3 mirror before selecting this alternative. The owner-linked 1806080392.pdf is now unavailable; this mirror is not proven byte-identical. AM26C31 is a proposed four-channel 16-pin line-driver on an external adapter; its one common 0 V must be confirmed compatible with all four SmoothieBox DRVX/DRVZ GND fields. No 24 V pulse terminals, high-speed terminals or CN1 digital GND are joined to these differential pairs. Both enable pins select active outputs while 5 V is present; proposed 10 kΩ input pull-downs prevent floating CMOS inputs but do not constitute a safety stop, and rail ramp/boot/reset/disconnect pulse behavior requires bench proof with the motors inhibited. TI specifies 4.5–5.5 V supply, VIH≥2 V, VIL≤0.8 V, recommended ±20 mA output and a nearby 0.1 µF bypass. Manufacturer CN1 opto input with two 120 Ω resistors is shown in printed p.38; output current, polarity, edge timing, 500 kHz maximum, cable, EMC and receiver fit require measurement; no claim that the shown driver is automatically electrically qualified. P01-01=0, P03-00=0, P03-01=1, P03-02=0 are manufacturer position/STEP-DIR/low-speed selections, not fitted settings. DRVX/DRVZ ENABLE fields remain unconnected here; Servo ON is a distinct 24 V DI circuit. CN1 contact numbers below are manufacturer table positions only; no fabricated shell face/cavity geometry.

wire_panels.title: CONDITIONAL X/Z JASD v1.3 Servo ON · complete ULN2003AN / AQY212GS isolated 24 V process interface
wire_panels.note: MANUFACTURER CONDITIONAL PROCESS-ENABLE EXAMPLE, not a fitted Servo ON or safety circuit. The exact fitted drive must match the JASD v1.3 manual and each axis must read back P06-01=1 (DI1 Servo ON) with P06-00=0 (active low / optocoupler-on) before the contact path is selected. External qualified +24 V feeds each CN1.11 COM+; each CN1.9 DI1− returns through its own normally-open AQY212GS SOP4 contact to external 24 V 0 V. A single ULN2003AN channels 1 and 2 sinks two current-limited AQY LEDs from the independently qualified adapter +5 V rail. 390 Ω LED series resistor and 10 kΩ DRV ENABLE input pull-down per axis are proposed design values, not fitted parts; measure LED current over rail and temperature tolerance (Panasonic recommended 5–10 mA), ULN saturation, AQY contact off leakage/on resistance against actual JASD DI1 response, and SmoothieBox DRVX/DRVZ ENABLE logic voltage/current/polarity/boot/reset/disconnect before connection. ULN unused inputs 3–7 are defined low at logic ground; unused collector outputs 10–14 and clamp COM9 remain NC for LED loads. The separate AQY contact side is not bonded in this proposal to controller/ULN 0 V, pulse negatives, analog ground or PE; cabinet bonds must be traced because device isolation alone does not prove system isolation. This process Servo ON command does not replace independent E-stop, STO, brake, contactor or overtravel safety. CN1.17 +24 V auxiliary, CN1.45/.47/.49 COM returns, 24 V pulse alternatives and analog input are unused in this conditional process circuit; source inventory lists all 50 CN1 terminals without a fabricated connector face.

wire_panels.title: CONDITIONAL Lenze8214 isolated spindle speed · native PWM → low-pass → isolated0–10V
wire_panels.note: Conditional design only: identify fitted drive and isolator revisions, verify Lenze0–10V jumper, measured PWM amplitude/frequency and startup defaults, low-pass component tolerances/loading/settling, configured voltage output and full-scale calibration. Manufacturer isolation rating must suit actual common-mode/cabinet; no reference bond across barrier or to Lenze39. Qualify open/short/power-loss behavior with drive inhibited before use. Native0–5V PWM uses carrier spindle connector, not a raw3.3V pin. 10kΩ/4.7µF is a proposed first-order passive filter; actualPWM≥20kHz and input>1Mohm are conditions, not fitted measurements. Factory isolator all-off config is CURRENT output0–20mA, not voltage: explicitly select/read back0–5V input and0–10V voltageoutput. Nominal24V power3/4 remains separate from signalinput1/2 and output5/6;7/8 are internally duplicatepower, not signal returns. Lenze7 GND1 must not be merged with39 GND2. This speed circuit does not include RUN/DIR or replace machine safety. Remaining Lenze terminals belong to separate digital/power inventories. Independent static review finds nominal47ms time constant, about216ms to1percent and ideal2.66mV peak-to-peak output ripple at20kHz/half duty. Loading permits approximately9.90V full-scale before module errors, so measure and calibrate rather than promise10V. An open resistor/reference can float the filter; an open capacitor removes filtering; charged capacitor can command speed on restart. Keep drive enable independently inhibited until valid zero command and stop behavior are established. This circuit is not fail-safe.

wire_panels.title: CONDITIONAL Lenze 8214 digital RUN/DIR · SmoothieBox → ULN2003AN → two Phoenix 24 V gold-signal relays
wire_panels.note: OWNER-REPORTED DRIVE FAMILY / CONDITIONAL MANUFACTURER INTERFACE, not verified fitted nameplate or cabinet continuity. Owner post #338649 names Lenze 8214, terminal 28 enable, E4 direction, 39 digital reference and reports original Mesa connections. Manufacturer 8200 SHB 0199 indexed text (printed pp.4-38/4-40/4-41) gives terminal 28 and E4 HIGH 12–30 V, LOW 0–3 V; 39 is GND2, distinct from analog GND1 terminal 7. A separate nominal 24 V field supply (within the 12–30 V high range) feeds Phoenix PLC-RSC-24DC/21AU 2966265 intact-gold contacts 11→14; each Lenze input has a proposed 10 kΩ pull-down to digital 39 so an open NO contact has a defined LOW and a closed contact has ~2.4 mA resistor current at 24 V before input current, within the manufacturer's 1 mA minimum at 24 V / 50 mA maximum / 36 V DC maximum only if actual measured contact current and voltage meet the intact-gold ratings. The two Phoenix coils are separate host-side nominal 24 V loads at A1/A2, driven by ULN2003AN collectors 16/15; integrated freewheel/polarity diodes are source-confirmed, so observe A1-positive/A2-sink and do not add an invented external diode. Their 18.5–33.6 V 20°C coil operating range and typical 9 mA are source values, not host supply proof. Native SmoothieBox SSR1.1/.2 RUN and PWM.2 TTL/PWM.3 DIRECTION assignments are candidates: their actual output level/current, firmware mapping, polarity, turn-on/off and boot/reset/disconnect behavior must be measured before use. Two proposed 10 kΩ logic input pull-downs and ULN inputs 3–7 tied low leave unused collectors 10–14 and COM9 NC. Relay terminal 12 NC is unused. Phoenix's safe-isolation rating is a component source claim, not qualification of this fitted cabinet common-mode, installation or safety function. No host logic 0 V, coil 24 V return, field digital 39, analog 7, cabinet PE or Lenze internal terminal 20 is joined by label. E4 is factory CW LOW / CCW HIGH in the manual but programmable; verify fitted configuration and actual spindle rotation with independent safe stop. Process RUN/DIR relays do not replace hardwired E-stop, brake, contactor or protection. Manufacturer PDF bytes were not locally recovered (direct HTTP403); cited terminal claims are from indexed text, so final fitment and manual readback remain mandatory. Field 10 kΩ resistors are proposed at ≥0.25 W, with measured thermal margin; 30 V across 10 kΩ dissipates 0.09 W before tolerance. Do not change direction while RUN is asserted: command zero, verify standstill using the fitted drive procedure, inhibit RUN, set direction, and enable only after the qualified relay settling interval. Independent direction relay supply loss or disconnect may select CW while RUN remains asserted. Qualification must establish fault detection and drive inhibit before direction-control faults or changes, including relay bounce, settling and restart interlock. This proposed topology alone does not enforce that interlock. Verify coil pickup after ULN saturation and suppression transients over rated temperature/supply bounds; validate minimum contact switching load at the actual field voltage.

Owner post #259199 (2022-12-11) explicitly reports “I am running JMC drives in analog mode.” It does not name the exact drive models or terminal pins. parts: No replacement part selected: identify exact JMC drive model/firmware and VFD model/manual before selecting signal interfaces.

Migration option A: if exact installed JMC drives support pulse-position mode, verify its terminals, differential/single-ended levels, timing, encoder/fault and control-loop behavior before considering Core.

Migration option B: if those drives cannot safely run from a compatible pulse-position controller, retain a supported closed-loop motion controller/servo architecture rather than assume a Smoothie analog position loop.
If spindle conversion is later considered, select a specific isolated analog-output plus enable/run interface from the exact VFD terminal schedule; preserve physical controls/E-stop.
instructions: Record exact Mesa boards, JMC model labels/manual revisions, servo/encoder labels, VFD label/parameter setup, CPV manifold, brake, relay board, contactors and safety wiring.
Use owner statement that the installed JMC drives are in analog mode as the control baseline. Inspect the current drive mode; do not generalize between JMC models.

Check the exact JMC manual for supported analog and pulse-position modes. The forum links a JMC servo-drive PDF at post #259363, but without the installed model label it cannot be bound to this machine. Only proceed with Core if the exact drive can be deliberately reconfigured and the complete drive/controller loop is supported; otherwise retain a supported closed-loop controller.
Resolve the reported M3/M4 behavior against current HAL/INI before claiming spindle control. Pin 28 is only a reported VFD enable terminal reference; verify model and function.
Bench-check any VFD converter isolated from machine power; validate 0-10V range only if model manual proves it, common, run/enable logic, deceleration/brake and fail-safe state.
Do not reconnect servos or VFD from a generic pin map. Confirm encoder feedback and independent safety before operation.
Only change backgear with spindle stopped under independent permissive; verify engagement mechanically because owner reports no gear-position sensor.
